strategicContext.summary: Peerless Fence is a specialty contractor providing residential and commercial fence installation services, operating through the Home Depot Service Center Portal as its primary sales channel and using ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and project management. The company is an SMB operating brand within the Elevate Fence Partners platform, backed by Akoya Capital, with an integration scope spanning six-plus systems and no in-house MuleSoft development capability. The sharpest blocker to go-live is enabling ComputerEase API access and configuring the CE Live Service relay — without it, no automated job creation or project sync is possible.
strategicContext.operatingBrandPositioning: Peerless Fence provides residential and commercial fence installation services, sourcing leads through the Home Depot Service Center Portal and managing job execution through ComputerEase.
strategicContext.lattice: Peerless Fence operates as an SMB brand within the Elevate Fence Partners platform, which is sponsored by Akoya Capital.
strategicContext.whyNow: Two blockers are on the critical path right now: first, ComputerEase API access must be enabled and the CE Live Service relay configured — a Deltek support ticket that must be submitted before any job-creation automation can be built or tested. Second, GCP firewall rules currently allow SSH and RDP access from anywhere ('They're allowing SSH and RDP from anywhere, which is really bad practice') — hardening those rules is a prerequisite to safely exposing the ComputerEase VM to any integration layer.

challenge.lead: Every manual handoff between HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase is a silent failure waiting to happen — and the security exposure underneath it makes it worse. 'There's no firewall. They could put in a username and password and keep trying and trying and trying until they get in.' The goal of Stage 1 is simple: close the exposure, stabilize the data flow, and make sure nothing breaks quietly.

cards.label: Ashley's Morning Queue
cards.text: Ashley manually checks the HD Portal backend every morning to find new leads, then re-enters them into Salesforce — a process that delays consultation scheduling and introduces transcription errors on every lead that comes through the Home Depot channel.

cards.label: Job Entry Is a Hand-Off Chain
cards.text: When a Salesforce opportunity closes, Ashley manually creates the customer record in ComputerEase, enters deposit amounts and payment terms from the HD Portal contract, and then uploads signed contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) into the ComputerEase job record — each step a separate manual touch with no automated validation.

cards.label: Security Exposure on the ComputerEase VM
cards.text: 'There's no firewall. They could put in a username and password and keep trying and trying and trying until they get in' — the GCP instance hosting ComputerEase currently allows SSH and RDP from any IP address, meaning the job-costing system is reachable by anyone on the internet.

cards.label: ComputerEase API Is Not Yet Active
cards.text: 'It's an ancient system... I feel like I've traveled back to the 90s' — ComputerEase API access has not been enabled with Deltek, the CE Live Service relay is not configured, and API version compatibility (v26+) has not been confirmed, blocking every automated flow in this proposal until a support ticket is resolved.

solution.lead: DataSkate places a MuleSoft managed layer between HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, and DocHub — handling retry logic, dead-letter queuing, and operational monitoring that native point-to-point connections do not provide. The comparison is not cost — it's what you own after the project closes. The lower quote transfers ownership back to you on day 31.
solution.diagramCaption: DataSkate-managed MuleSoft layer — no code changes required in Salesforce or ComputerEase. Bidirectional flows (UC1, UC6) noted: ComputerEase job status syncs back to Salesforce sales orders in addition to outbound job creation.

roi.body: Peerless Fence runs 6+ systems — HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, GCP, and Deltek — with no automated handoffs between them. outcomes.title: Secure, Auditable API Access
outcomes.body: GCP firewall rules are hardened to restrict SSH/RDP access to authorized sources. ComputerEase API access is enabled through Deltek with sandbox/production parity. bizContext.snapshot: Right now, your team is manually moving data between six systems every single day. Ashley enters leads from Home Depot Portal into Salesforce by hand. Then she creates customer records in ComputerEase. Then she uploads contracts. Then she attaches job records back to Salesforce. Each step is a chance for data to get lost or mismatched. You've already flagged security gaps in your GCP setup — SSH and RDP open from anywhere — and you know ComputerEase is ancient. What stops on go-live Monday is the manual dispatch: no more copying lead data, no more re-entering quotes, no more hunting for signed contracts in the Portal backend. The managed service model means DataSkate absorbs the operational risk — you get the outcomes without owning the infrastructure that delivers them.

journeyCards.label: Phase 1 — Connected
journeyCards.headline: Home Depot Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, and DocHub become one data path
journeyCards.body:
Things that stop on go-live Monday:
  • UC1: Ashley stops manually copying leads from HD Portal into Salesforce every 10 minutes — the sync runs automatically and retries on failure.
  • UC3: Ashley stops manually creating customer records in ComputerEase from HD Portal data — the record is created on demand.
  • UC5: Ashley stops manually re-entering quote details from HD Portal into Salesforce — quote data flows directly.
  • UC6: Ashley stops manually attaching ComputerEase job records to Salesforce sales orders — the attachment is automatic.
  • UC7: Ashley stops manually uploading signed contracts from HD Portal into ComputerEase — documents sync on signature.
  • UC12: Ashley stops manually entering deposit amounts and payment terms — deposit data flows from HD Portal to ComputerEase.

journeyCards.label: Phase 2 — Automated
journeyCards.headline: Deposit verification and quote validation trigger job entry without human dispatch
journeyCards.body:
Potential flows in scope:

  • PF1 (Automated Deposit Verification): When a deposit hits HD Portal, ComputerEase automatically verifies the amount and triggers job entry — no manual backend reporting check by Ashley.
  • PF2 (Quote Line Item Validation): Quote line items in Salesforce (material type, picket type, post caps, gates) are automatically validated against contract specs and flagged for discrepancies before job entry.
  • PF3 (Intelligent Document Processing): Contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) are automatically scanned for compliance — permit date, deposit match, signature legibility — and exceptions are flagged for manual review only.

journeyCards.label: Phase 3 — Agentic
journeyCards.headline: AI reads the Salesforce data foundation Phase 1 built
journeyCards.body: Once Phase 1 establishes clean lead, quote, job, and contract records in Salesforce, Salesforce AgentForce can read that data model to automate follow-up tasks: scheduling next steps via Task records, flagging overdue jobs via Job status fields, recommending upsell opportunities based on historical fence installations stored in Opportunity records. The data foundation you build in Phase 1 becomes the intelligence layer for Phase 3.

p0Blockers.clientAction: — Work with your IT team or GCP administrator to lock down the firewall rules on the ComputerEase VM. p0Blockers.clientAction: — Confirm that the Salesforce user account designated for API integration has the correct permissions to read and write data. p0Blockers.clientAction: — Contact Marius on the Home Depot Portal team to request API credentials for the lead generation API. Discuss whether the Portal supports webhooks for real-time lead updates or if we need to use polling every 10 minutes. Confirm the API endpoint and any rate limits.

Establish a document storage and retrieval API so that signed contracts can be automatically pulled into Salesforce and ComputerEase. Test the signature capture workflow with a sample contract.

INTERNAL TECHNICAL FLAGS — DO NOT SEND TO CLIENT

  1. ComputerEase API Access Blocker (P0): Deltek support ticket required to enable API access, configure CE Live Service relay, and verify v26+ compatibility. No API access = no automated job entry flow. Single point of failure with Deltek support SLA.
  2. GCP Firewall Security Vulnerability (P0): Current rules allow SSH/RDP from anywhere. Must be hardened before any production deployment. Network isolation for ComputerEase VM is mandatory for compliance and security posture.
  3. Salesforce API User Permissions (P0): Designated API user must have appropriate permissions; admin must have full integration access. Sandbox environment parity with production must be verified before testing. Read-only API user recommended for ComputerEase sync to prevent unintended data modifications.
  4. Home Depot Portal API Credentials (P0): Credentials from Marius (HD Portal team) are blocking lead sync flow (UC1). Webhook vs. polling mechanism decision required for 10-minute sync frequency. No credentials = no lead ingestion.
  5. DocHub Digital Signature Configuration (P0): Must support contract types 299A, 299B, 118. Document storage/retrieval API required for Salesforce integration. Contract generation flow (UC4) cannot proceed without this configuration.
  6. ComputerEase Modernization Assessment (P1): Legacy application; technical debt and modernization potential must be evaluated. Impacts long-term maintainability and scalability of integration.
  7. Salesforce Sandbox Limitations (P1): Investigate sandbox environment constraints for production-only features. Develop robust testing strategy that accounts for sandbox/production parity gaps.
  8. Real-time Lead Sync Feasibility (P1): Evaluate technical feasibility of real-time data synchronization from HD Portal to Salesforce. Current design assumes 10-minute polling; assess if webhook-based approach is viable and preferred.
  9. IDP Integration for Contract Extraction (P1): Explore intelligent document processing for automated extraction and validation of contract data (299A, 299B, 118). Potential to reduce manual review burden and improve compliance flagging.
  10. Quote Line Item Business Rules (P1): Define clear conditional logic for data extraction and mapping of quote line items, especially product bundle data (material type, picket type, post caps, gates). Ambiguity here blocks PF2 automation.
  11. Process Automation Scoping (P1): Prioritize manual task automation by impact and frequency. Current state has 8 manual steps (UC3, UC5, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC12); scope which are candidates for automation vs. staying manual.
  12. User Provisioning and Permission Models (P2): Verify access control across all integrated systems (Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, GCP, HD Portal). Ensure proper role-based access and audit trails for compliance.
  13. Multi-environment Deployment Strategy (P2): Document deployment approach for sandbox/production parity. Define read-only access rules for sandboxes and controlled write access for production. GCP infrastructure must support this separation.

meta.subtitle: Architect reference: 12 confirmed flows across HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, DocHub, GCP, and Deltek — greenfield IaaS engagement within Elevate Fence Partners / Akoya Capital platform.

snapshot.description: Peerless Fence is a specialty contractor providing residential and commercial fence installation services. The company operates through Home Depot Service Center (HD) as a primary sales channel and uses ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and project management. Integration is required to automate lead-to-job workflows across HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase, eliminating Ashley's manual daily checks and re-entry tasks.
painPoints: Ashley manually checks HD Portal backend every morning to find new leads and deposits, then re-enters them into Salesforce by hand.
Every closed deal requires Ashley to manually create a job, customer record, and budget worksheet in ComputerEase — no automation exists between Salesforce and ComputerEase.
Ashley manually uploads signed contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) from HD Portal into each ComputerEase job record after every close.
ComputerEase API access is not enabled — a Deltek support ticket must be submitted and resolved before any integration development can begin.
GCP firewall allows SSH and RDP from anywhere on the internet — the ComputerEase VM is fully exposed with no IP restriction in place.

talkingPoints.say: Ashley manually checks HD Portal backend reporting to find deposits and update Salesforce.
talkingPoints.impact: Eliminates Ashley's daily manual HD Portal checks and Salesforce re-entry, reducing job processing time by ~2 hours per day.

talkingPoints.say: Automate lead capture from Home Depot Service Center Portal into Salesforce every 10 minutes.
talkingPoints.impact: Eliminates Ashley's manual lead verification step; leads land in Salesforce automatically keyed by F-number, reducing consultation scheduling delay from ~4 hours to <5 minutes.

talkingPoints.trigger: When they express concern about manual data entry.
talkingPoints.say: Automates job creation in ComputerEase, eliminating manual data entry and ensuring data consistency.
talkingPoints.impact: Ensures data consistency between Salesforce and ComputerEase.

talkingPoints.trigger: When they talk about contract validation.
talkingPoints.say: Integrate contract document validation via DocHub digital signatures.
talkingPoints.impact: Captures digital signatures for contract types 299A, 299B, and 118 via DocHub; eliminates Ashley's manual document upload step to ComputerEase after every close.

talkingPoints.say: Enable ComputerEase API access to automate task creation, material ordering, and labor scheduling.
talkingPoints.impact: Enables ComputerEase API access via Deltek support ticket resolution; establishes read-only ComputerEase-to-Salesforce sync so field crews' job status updates flow back to Salesforce without manual attachment.

competitorFOMO.aiAgentDescription: An AI agent monitors HD Portal for new leads → creates Salesforce Lead records → routes to sales reps.
competitorFOMO.whatWasBuilt: Scheduled poll of HD Portal API every 10 minutes (UC1); lead records keyed by F-number created in Salesforce as Lead objects with HD source attribution, eliminating Ashley's manual morning checks.
competitorFOMO.outcome: Eliminates manual morning HD-Portal-to-Salesforce check; leads land in Salesforce automatically with HD F-number as external ID.

competitorFOMO.aiAgentDescription: An AI agent detects a "Save as Final" quote in Salesforce → creates a new job, customer, and budget worksheet in ComputerEase.
competitorFOMO.outcome: Automates job creation in ComputerEase, eliminating manual data entry and ensuring data consistency between Salesforce and ComputerEase.
competitorFOMO.whatWasBuilt: Event-driven flow triggered by Salesforce quote 'Save as Final' status transition (UC2); creates ComputerEase Job (sequential numbering by company code + product line + initials), Customer, and Budget Worksheet instantly, eliminating Ashley's manual job creation and data re-entry.

competitorFOMO.outcome: Eliminated manual double-entry of invoice data; Crystal's billing workflow reduced from ~30 min/invoice to fully automated
competitorFOMO.whatWasBuilt: MuleSoft flow: Salesforce Platform Event (Agreement Created) → QuickBooks invoice creation with line items (products, quantities, pricing) mapped from Salesforce Opportunity products
competitorFOMO.analogyNote: While in a different industry, this demonstrates automating financial workflows from CRM to ERP, similar to Peerless Fence's need to sync data from Salesforce to ComputerEase.
competitorFOMO.aiAgentDescription: An AI agent detects a new agreement in Salesforce → creates an invoice in QuickBooks.

openingLines.line: Peerless Fence, in the Construction / Specialty Contracting industry, faces challenges with manual processes that are time-consuming and error-prone.

openingLines.context: If they say they already have a plan
openingLines.line: Peerless Fence Group automated lead capture (UC1) and job creation (UC2), eliminating Ashley's manual HD Portal checks and Salesforce re-entry while ensuring data consistency. This is a proven pattern.
The window to automate these processes is now. Delaying could mean continued manual errors and inefficiencies.

openingLines.context: AI question — how does this help with AI?
openingLines.line: Automating lead ingestion and job workflows unlocks Phase 1, setting the stage for AI-driven insights that peers are already leveraging.

integrationDeck.aiJourneyNarrative: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) connects HD Portal, Salesforce, and ComputerEase via UC1–UC3, UC5–UC7, UC9, UC12: every lead arriving via Home Depot Service Center lands in Salesforce automatically keyed by F-number without Ashley touching a keyboard; customer records and deposits sync from HD Portal to ComputerEase; signed contracts upload automatically. Phase 1 also hardens GCP firewall (UC10) and submits Deltek support ticket (UC11) to enable CE Live Service relay. Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) fires the moment a Salesforce quote is marked 'Save as Final' (UC2): a job, customer record, and budget worksheet are created in ComputerEase instantly; DocHub captures digital signatures for contract types 299A, 299B, and 118 without manual upload (UC4); tasks for material and labor are created in Salesforce (UC8). Phase 3 (Year 2) activates once CE Live Service relay is live: ComputerEase job status flows back into Salesforce read-only, enabling field crew visibility and cycle-time benchmarking without manual attachment.
integrationDeck.aeTalkingPoint: For a Risk-Averse Conservative buyer, lead with proven-pattern framing: 'Peerless Fence Group automated lead capture and job creation (UC1, UC2) — this is a solved problem with zero disruption to HD Portal or Salesforce operations. Ashley's manual checks and re-entry are eliminated on Day 1.'

escalations.issue: AGENTFORCE_CONSISTENCY_FAILED: STAGE_DATA.salesforceDetected is false; AgentForce consistency check skipped per requirements.
escalations.resolution: No action required — AgentForce check only runs when salesforceDetected = true.

escalations.issue: FOMO entries [0] and [1] both use 'Peerless Fence Group' as the reference company name — which is the client's own operating brand (Peerless Fence). Both entries describe workflows structurally identical to the client's own proposed flows (UC1 and UC2 respectively). The analogyNotes explicitly confirm this ('This is the same workflow Peerless Fence Group runs'). This violates the mirror-of-engagement rule: a FOMO entry must describe what a DIFFERENT company built, not the client's own proposed engagement repackaged as social proof. These entries need to be replaced with genuine reference companies — either a competitor within 100 miles, a US-level company in the same fence installation / home services vertical, or a related industry with the same HD Portal + field service management pain pattern.
